title: Chemical Reactions
standard_text: The five types of chemical reactions (synthesis, decomposition, single displacement, double displacement, combustion); balancing equations; the activity series; neutralization; naming and writing formulas for compounds. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Chemistry, Grade 11, University Preparation (SCH3U), Strand C: Chemical Reactions)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Chemistry (SCH3U) worksheets on chemical reactions: synthesis, decomposition, single and double displacement, combustion, balancing equations, the activity series and neutralization. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed: balance every equation.
key_sub: Synthesis, decomposition, single and double displacement, combustion.
body_html:
How to think about it

Classify a reaction by its pattern: A + B → AB (synthesis), AB → A + B (decomposition), A + BC → AC + B (single displacement), AB + CD → AD + CB (double displacement) and fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O (combustion of a hydrocarbon).

A single displacement happens only if the free element is more reactive than the one it replaces (check the activity series). A double displacement happens if a precipitate, a gas or water forms. Balance by changing coefficients, never subscripts.

Example

Zn + CuSO₄ → ? Will it react?

Zinc is above copper in the activity series.

Answer: yes: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu

Example

Balance: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O

2 O on the left, so 2 H₂O

Then 4 H, so 2 H₂

Answer: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O

Common mistakes

  • Changing a subscript to balance an equation, which makes a different substance.
  • Writing hydrogen or oxygen as single atoms (H, O) instead of H₂ and O₂.
  • Predicting a single displacement when the free metal is less reactive.

faq.a: A double displacement between an acid and a base that makes a salt and water.

items.q: Is this equation balanced? 2H<sub>2</sub> + 4O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O
c: No. O has 8 atoms on the left and 2 on the right.
Yes. Both sides have the same elements.
No. There are too many arrows.
items.e: Count each element on both sides.

items.q: Using the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au), which metal is more reactive: calcium or lead?
items.e: Higher in the list = loses electrons more easily.

items.q: A piece of gold is placed in lead(II) nitrate solution. Will a displacement reaction occur? (Reactivity series: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au)
c: No. Metals never react with solutions.
Yes. Any metal replaces any other metal.
Yes. Gold is more active than lead, so it replaces it.
No. Gold is less active than lead, so no reaction occurs.
items.e: A metal replaces only metals below it in the reactivity series.

Carbon is more reactive than zinc.
Zinc is above carbon in the series.

items.q: What are the products when iron reacts with sulfuric acid?
c: iron(II) sulfate, water and carbon dioxide
items.e: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen.

items.q: Zinc carbonate reacts with nitric acid. What are the products?

items.e: acid + base → salt + water; acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.

items.q: Is sodium chloride soluble or insoluble in water?
items.e: All Na, K and ammonium salts and all nitrates are soluble; chlorides are soluble except AgCl and PbCl₂; sulfates except BaSO₄, PbSO₄ and CaSO₄; carbonates are insoluble except Na, K and ammonium.

sets.title: Names, formulas and evidence of reactions

items.q: A glass bottle is crushed into small pieces. What kind of change is this?
c: a chemical change, because new substances form
a physical change, because the substance stays the same
items.e: No new substance forms.

items.q: What is the name of CaCl<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: What is the name of BaS?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: How many atoms of Fe are in 2Fe?
items.e: 2Fe: the coefficient 2 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: How many atoms of N are in 2NO?
items.e: 2NO: the coefficient 2 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: How many atoms of O are in 3O<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 3O<sub>2</sub>: the coefficient 3 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 3 × 2 = 6.

items.q: How many atoms of C are in 3CO<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: 3CO<sub>2</sub>: the coefficient 3 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 3 × 1 = 3.

items.q: A clear solution turns cloudy and a yellow solid forms when two solutions mix. What kind of change is this?

items.e: Evidence: gas, precipitate, colour change, light or temperature change from a reaction.
